abstract_kind: opening
significance: "In this book review of the second edition of Dale and Fortin's Spatial Analysis: A Guide for Ecologists, I find a better laid-out, updated and well-referenced overview of classic spatial methods, but little broadening of its methodological scope. I argue that the book should have given more room to the move towards fitting explicit, often hierarchical spatial models with Bayesian inference and modern numerical methods, and that a more applied, computational focus would make it more useful for self-study. I nevertheless see no alternative for a theoretically solid yet accessible overview of classic spatial methods in ecology, and point readers to complementary texts on implementation, point patterns and hierarchical modelling."

## Opening paragraph

<p>It may be too early to call “Spatial Analysis – A Guide for Ecologists” by Fortin and Dale a modern classic, but since its publication in 2005 the book has certainly become a widely cited reference in the field of spatial ecology. Cambridge University Press has now published a second edition of this introductory textbook.</p>
